chunks: Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from ʿĪsā ibn Ayyūb, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

There is no servant except that in his heart there is a white spot. So when he commits a sin, a black spot appears within that spot. If he repents, that blackness goes away; but if he persists in sins, that blackness increases until it covers the whiteness. Then when it has covered the whiteness, its possessor never returns to any good, ever.
And this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted upon their hearts.”

key_terms.تَابَ: he repented and returned from sin
key_terms.قَلْبِهِ: his heart, the inner spiritual faculty
key_terms.نُكْتَةٌ بَيْضَاءُ: a white spot symbolizing original purity and receptivity to good
key_terms.نُكْتَةٌ سَوْدَاءُ: a black spot signifying the spiritual effect of sin
key_terms.يَكْسِبُونَ: they used to earn through their deeds

ai.seo_question: How do sins and repentance affect the heart in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the heart is originally marked by purity, but each sin leaves a dark effect upon it. Repentance removes that stain, while persistence in sin causes spiritual hardening until the heart is covered over, which the Imam عليه السلام connects to the Quranic description of rust upon hearts.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Isa Bin Ayoub, fromAli Bin Mahziyar, from Al Qasim Bin Urwat, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is none from a servant except that there is a white spot in his heart. So when he commits a sin, a black spot appears in the (white) spot. So if he repents, that (black spot) goes away, and if he deliberates in the sins, that black (spot) increases until it covers the white (spot). So when the white (spot) is covered upon, its owner would not return to the goodness, ever!
And these are the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [83:14] Nay! rather, what they used to do has become like rust upon their hearts’.
en.sarwar: 20. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from ‘Isa ibn Ayyub from Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from ibn Bukayr from Zurara from abu Ja’far who has said the following:

“In the heart of every servant (of Allah) there is a white dot. When he commits a sin a black dot appears in the white one. If he repents the black dot goes away, but if he continues committing sins the black dot enlarges until it covers the white dot and when the white dot is covered the person thereafter does not return to good things
as Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, ‘In fact, their hearts are stained by their deeds.’” ( 83 : 14 )
